display.title: In Every Generation: Feeling Our Own Exodus from Mitzrayim
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains the Pesach pasuk from the Twelve Pesukim, 'In every generation...', followed by a short skit about two children who free a trapped deer.
display.summary_long: A Pesach talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, broadcast during Chol HaMoed. Uncle Yossi reviews what we do at the Seder, matzah, maror, wine, reclining and the Haggadah, to show we are a free nation, and recalls that had Hashem not taken our fathers out of Egypt, we would still be slaves. He then teaches one of the Twelve Pesukim, 'In every generation a person must see himself as if he left Mitzrayim': the Exodus happened more than 3,300 years ago, yet its miracles and freedom are ours today, so we read the Haggadah as the story of our own redemption. A short dramatized skit follows: Dovid and his sister, dreaming in their pajamas, wander into 'Mitzvah Stone National Park' and free a deer stuck in a bush; the deer's relief reminds them how the Jewish people were stuck as slaves in Egypt until Hashem took them out, and that we should thank Hashem and remember the Exodus every day.
display.lesson: The freedom of Pesach is our own; we should feel as if we ourselves left Mitzrayim and thank Hashem every day.
